sections.h2: How does property tax work in Boone County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Boone County property is valued by the county Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), billed by the Boone County Sheriff, and taxed by several overlapping districts. The PVA sets the assessment as of January 1, and the sheriff mails and collects the bill in the fall.

Boone is the northernmost county in Kentucky, a 256 square mile county on the Ohio River across from Cincinnati. Burlington is the county seat and Florence is the largest city, with Union and Walton the other incorporated cities. The bill you receive is built from a state rate, a county rate, a city rate where one applies, and separate rates for the library, health department, extension office, fire district and school district, so two houses in the same county can carry different totals.

If you plan to sell, the useful question is who owes which year. Kentucky taxes are measured on the January 1 owner, so a bill that arrives in September or October may carry the name of the person who held the house in January, even if you now own it.

sections.h2: What is the Boone County collection schedule and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
For 2026 bills, the sheriff posted a discount window from October 1 through November 1, face amount from November 2 through December 31, and escalating penalties after that. The statute behind the pattern is KRS 134.015, so the same calendar repeats each year unless the state approves a delayed schedule.

Boone County Sheriff collection schedule posted for 2026 bills
WindowAmount due
October 1 to November 1, 2026Bill less a 2 percent discount
November 2 to December 31, 2026Face amount
January 1 to January 31, 2027Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15, 202710 percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff add-on

Source: Boone County Sheriff property tax notice.

The sheriff does not accept partial payments, so a bill is paid in full or not at all. Online card payments carry a vendor fee, and e-checks carry a smaller flat fee. The sheriff's office is on Conrad Lane in Burlington, and the notice lists extended Saturday hours in October. Tax bills are mailed by the end of September.

sections.h2: What happens to a Boone County tax bill that goes unpaid?
sections.html:
At the close of business on April 15, an unpaid bill moves from the sheriff to the Boone County Clerk and becomes a certificate of delinquency with a lien recorded against the property. The 2026 notice puts that transfer at April 15, 2027.

Once the clerk holds the bill, the cost jumps. The sheriff's notice lists a 20 percent county attorney fee, a 10 percent clerk fee and interest at 1 percent per month on top of the earlier penalties. The Department of Revenue explains that unpaid certificates can then be offered to a third party buyer at a summer sale, after which you deal with that buyer and its added fees.

  • The lien follows the parcel. Under KRS 134.015, it lasts until the tax is paid or 11 years pass, whoever owns the house.
  • Notices go to the owner of record, so an old mailing address can mean you never see the warning.
  • Payment plans are possible through the county attorney according to the Department of Revenue, so call early.

A house with a delinquent certificate can still be sold, but the title company will want the certificate paid from the proceeds, and the amount due is quoted by the clerk, not the sheriff.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Boone County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference with the Boone County PVA, because Kentucky does not let you file an appeal until that conference has happened. The PVA's own page says the online appeal request is open from October 1 through May 1, and you can also email appeals@boonecountyky.org to book a conference.

The formal window is short. Under state law, the tax roll inspection period begins the first Monday in May and runs two weeks, ending on the third Monday. If the conference does not settle it, you file with the county clerk no later than one workday after the inspection period closes. The Boone PVA explains that you cannot appeal when the bill arrives, because assessments must be final before rates are calculated.

  • Bring sale prices of comparable homes close to yours, the way the PVA's own model works.
  • Bring photos or repair estimates if the condition is worse than a county record shows.
  • Ask for the sales list the PVA used on your parcel.

The local board of assessment appeals meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection closes under KRS 133.030, and a decision letter explains the next appeal step if you still disagree.

sections.h2: Why did my Boone County assessment go up?
sections.html:
Most increases come from sales. The Boone PVA says it values homes from nearby arm's length sales through a computer assisted system, and it inspects every parcel at least once every four years, so a jump often reflects several years of price growth landing at once.

The office also points to House Bill 44, which limits growth in countywide tax revenue to 4 percent a year. That law affects the tax rate, not the assessed value, so a rising valuation can come with a falling rate. The state requires mass appraisal results to fall within 90 to 110 percent of sales, a ratio test the PVA runs every year.

Census data helps explain the pressure. The 2020 count was 135,968 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 145,316, a 6.9 percent gain, in a county with 56,021 housing units. The median owner occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $277,300, and the median household income is $99,414, more than three times the figure reported for Bell County in southeast Kentucky.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Boone County homestead or disability exemption?
sections.html:
Owners who turn 65 during the tax year, or who are totally disabled, can have a fixed amount subtracted from the assessment. The Boone PVA lists the 2026 amount as $49,100, and the sheriff's notice says the figure should already appear on the front of a bill if the PVA has your application.

  • You must own the home and live in it as your residence on January 1.
  • Only one exemption is allowed per household, even if both spouses qualify.
  • Disabled owners under 65 reapply every year, except service connected disabled veterans and owners found permanently disabled under Social Security or state retirement rules.
  • The exemption belongs to the owner. When you sell, the PVA moves it off the old address and the buyer applies on their own.

If the amount is missing from your bill, call the PVA before you pay. KRS 132.810 gives you a refund of the tax on the exempt value if you qualify after paying, but fixing it first is simpler. Applications go to the PVA by mail, fax, email or online form.

sections.h2: What should a Boone County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
Expect the title company to pay the current tax bill from your proceeds and prorate it between you and the buyer. The PVA says that if you buy after January 1 the bill may still arrive in the previous owner's name, and the closing statement is where that adjustment is settled.

That has three practical effects for a seller. Check whether the bill for the year is paid or still open, and ask the sheriff for a duplicate if you never received it, since the sheriff cannot see new deed transfers. Confirm that a deed or other recorded document changes the owner name on the PVA record, because name changes are made there, not at the sheriff. And if you inherited the house, a death certificate can be submitted to the PVA to update the record.

Boone County sellers with a delinquent bill, a missing exemption or a house with deferred repairs often choose a direct cash sale because the buyer takes the house as it stands and the delinquent amount is paid from the proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Where are the Boone County offices?
sections.html:
Four offices handle the cycle. The PVA in Burlington values property and takes homestead and appeal requests at 859-334-2181. The Boone County Sheriff collects bills at 859-334-2175, with a payment portal at boonecountytax.com. The County Clerk records deeds, takes appeals and receives delinquent bills after April 15. Heritage Bank branches also accepted tax payments for the 2026 bills, according to the sheriff.

Boone is served mainly by Boone County Schools, with a portion in the Walton-Verona Independent district, so your school rate depends on which district the parcel sits in. Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport is in the county, and Census figures show transportation and warehousing receipts of about $1.87 billion for 2022.

faqs.q: When are Boone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Face amount is due between November 2 and December 31, with a 2 percent discount through November 1. For 2026 bills, the sheriff listed a 5 percent penalty in January 2027 and a 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent add-on from February 1 to April 15, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Boone County assessment after the bill arrives?
faqs.a: No. Appeals are tied to the May inspection period, which starts the first Monday in May and lasts two weeks. You must hold a conference with the PVA first, then file with the county clerk within one workday after the period closes.

faqs.q: How much is the Boone County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The Boone PVA lists $49,100 for 2026. It applies to owners who turn 65 in the tax year or who are totally disabled, and it comes off the assessment, not the bill itself.

faqs.q: Who gets the tax bill if I sold the house this year?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the January 1 owner. If you sold afterward, the buyer should forward it or call the sheriff for a copy, and the closing statement divides the cost between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Boone County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays on the parcel, so the unpaid amount, including any clerk and attorney fees, is normally paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Ask the sheriff or the clerk for the exact payoff before you set a price.
